ideas.title: Form the plates the way Plante did
ideas.critique: This is round 1's 'First lead plates fizz' again, but the written-in efficiencies are gone: the current splits between solid conversion and gassing by Butler-Volmer at each plate's own potential, so the fizz and the browning come out of the kinetics, and the player's reversals decide the capacity. That makes it a choice whose outcome the physics decides, and it is the big goal's core. The risk is the film: a jar on a bench browning while nobody is there is the island's most worn form ('Six clay pots', 'Sparks at dusk'). The leads swapping has to be something the player is seen doing, or the depth of the model never reaches anyone watching.

ideas.title: Stir the jar, the cart goes further
ideas.critique: Round 1's green cloud, now with advection and a verb. A participating medium whose density is the solved Fe2+ field is still a trick only a path tracer can play, and the cloud clearing as it swirls makes the film something that changes over time instead of a before/after still. The stick's swirl is a vortex typed into the field rather than a stick really moving the brine, which caps how real it is. It also tunes the pots, a source the accumulator is meant to replace, so it does little for the cart's evening run.

ideas.title: The cart runs on the formed plates
ideas.critique: Putting stored charge into the cart's circuit is exactly the step the goal needs. As pitched, though, it is a lumped cell (OCV from acid strength, R from plate area, capacity as one number) and distance as charge divided by draw, and the film is the cart-on-planks shot again, only faster, then stopping. It is only as good as the forming model behind it. Without that model the capacity is a number typed in, and the place where it stops is set before the cart leaves.
